A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe HybridDeepSearcher and HDS-QA. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching material across figure renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on five QA benchmarks, search-scaling and evidence-coverage results, ablations, and model-output case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, supplementary analyses, ablations, and case studies reported in v2.

M1.justification: The HDS-QA construction pipeline, supervised training, and reasoning–querying–retrieval procedure remain unchanged. The planning labels in new Figure 1 annotate existing reasoning from Appendix F rather than introduce a planning component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HDS-QA training and evaluation on MuSiQue, FanOutQA, FRAMES, MedBrowseComp, and BrowseComp†. New Figure 1 uses an existing FRAMES question rather than add task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, supplementary experiments, and case studies. Figure 1 redraws the existing Search-o1 comparison; its additional citation to Search-R1 does not establish a newly evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same evaluation samples, training split, backbones, metrics, hyperparameters, and search limits. The budget-constrained procedures in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The single-query and GRPO comparisons, budget analyses, evidence analyses, and model-size and summarizer ablations are retained. New Figure 1 redisplays the FRAMES case already documented in Tables 16 and 19, without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report four trajectory-generation attempts per question and the same descriptive statistics. Neither introduces evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and retained plots are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports HybridDeepSearcher F1 scores of 44.1 on FanOutQA and 15.1 on BrowseComp† in both versions. Figure 1 repeats the existing Starman versus Elvis case outcomes.

T1.justification: The AUC and evidence-coverage definitions remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about hybrid supervision, search scaling, efficiency, and evidence coverage. The introductory illustration does not redefine the central contributions or performance claims.

C2.justification: New Figure 1 explicitly attributes previous methods' incomplete coverage to redundant sequential searches without explicit planning, while labeling the proposed model's reasoning as planning. This adds a limited mechanism interpretation; the blanket absence-of-planning characterization is stronger than the retained Search-o1 trace in Table 19 supports.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, training time, hyperparameters, retrieval and summarization instructions, Appendix E prompts, and the project-link disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are unchanged. However, new Figure 1 locally strengthens the contrast with Search-o1 and Search-R1 by characterizing earlier methods as lacking explicit planning, adding a limited research-positioning claim.

P1.justification: The introduction and search-scaling caption receive limited wording edits to incorporate the new illustration. Figure references are updated, while section ordering and nearly all substantive prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a side-by-side search-behavior schematic as Figure 1 and wraps introductory text around it. Existing figures are renumbered, Table 2 moves from page 7 to page 8, and several captions become smaller. Existing plots and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: New Figure 1 makes the existing Appendix F comparison easier to grasp by juxtaposing repetitive sequential queries with parallel retrieval across 12 films. This provides a small explanatory gain without changing the scientific evidence or reproducibility. The benefit is tempered by its broad absence-of-planning claim, since Table 19 already shows Search-o1 stating an initial plan.
